# Decision catalog (auto-generated)

Read first. Then read `decisions/<slug>.md` for the full body. Generated by execute-plan when a plan touches `decisions/`. Do not edit by hand — changes will be overwritten.

## Decisions

- `acquire-prefix-fallback` — Acquisition-failure policy lookup falls back exact producer class → `acquire/*` family → unknown-class default.
- `acquire-unavailable-carveout` — The acquire-unavailable handler is the single named carve-out from the unified resolution engine, deterministically injection-tested.
- `advisory-locks` — Postgres advisory locks plus a SQLite equivalent at session level.
- `artifact-layout` — Per-run directory at `<root>/.rimsky/runs/<timestamp>-<name>/` containing `state.db` and `blobs/`; `latest` symlink.
- `artifact-root-discovery` — Walk up from cwd for the first `.rimsky/`; create in cwd otherwise; `--workdir` overrides.
- `async-callback-outcome-oneof` — Oneof `success` | `error` | `park` plus optional `events` array; exactly one outcome key.
- `async-callback-post-json` — HTTP POST with JSON `AsyncCallbackBody` to the per-ack callback path under the control-API versioned prefix.
- `auth-anonymous-via-empty-key-ledger` — Rely on the existing anonymous-mode rule for loopback admission in one-shot runs; the verb provisions no keys.
- `auth-api-key-bearer` — Api-key as bearer token.
- `auth-dry-run-mode-floor-on-key` — A grant's `mode: dry_run` pins a key to dry-run regardless of the request flag.
- `auth-dry-run-request-flag` — A `?dry_run=true` query flag on writes.
- `auth-grant-scope` — A `scope` map of action-specific dimension keys (e.g., `template_tag`) constraining the action.
- `blessed-invariant-annotations` — `@blessed-invariant` blocks naming the property plus its enforcement site; scenario tests exercise them.
- `blob-backend` — One-shot mode uses the filesystem blob backend rooted at the per-run blob dir with the default spill threshold.
- `blob-backends-pluggable` — Pluggable backend interface with inline, postgres-large-object, filesystem, and in-memory implementations.
- `blob-spill-threshold-config` — Configurable byte threshold per deployment; default inline-only.
- `build-cgo-disabled` — CGO disabled for all builds.
- `build-go-version` — Go 1.25.0 minimum.
- `build-tool-makefile` — The build orchestration as single source of truth.
- `carry-verbatim-requires-one` — The carry-verbatim aggregation policy requires exactly one child, enforced at template validation.
- `cascade-flags-on-subscribes` — The cascade-behavior flags `wake_on_change` and `force_upstream_refresh` are fields of the subscription-entry shape, not of the substitution-ref shape and not of a separate block.
- `cascade-flags-required-no-defaults` — Both `wake_on_change` and `force_upstream_refresh` are required on every subscription entry; registration rejects entries missing either, and no defaults are applied.
- `cascade-inside-settlement` — The parent-settlement cascade bridge fires within the settle-children primitive, not at call sites.
- `child-execution-naming` — The primitive pair is named dispatch-children / settle-children.
- `child-execution-unification` — One dispatch-children plus one settle-children primitive serve both delegation and fan-out; the parallel implementations are deleted.
- `claimant-guard-helper` — Each persistence driver routes claimant-guarded mutations through one internal helper that appends the guard predicate.
- `cli-verb` — New `rimsky compose run <manifest>` sub-verb sibling to `up | down | plan | status`.
- `coding-style` — Rimsky's coding methodology is Plumbline; all three lint checks active (`source_validity`, `blessed_invariant_test_coverage`, `comment_hygiene`) with GoDoc/JSDoc exemptions; PostToolUse + CI lint enforce.
- `comment-drift-sweep` — Comments that misdescribe their code are corrected as defects, not tolerated as drift.
- `comment-hygiene-uniform-rule` — Comment-hygiene violations resolve per-site by tag-or-delete; the doc-residue cluster overrides with reshape-first.
- `compose-engine-reuse` — The one-shot verb reuses the existing compose engine via an HTTP client against the loopback control-api.
- `config-flip` — Activation of an inactive Plumbline check follows clean state — the flip is committed only after the codebase is clean against that check.
- `config-format-yaml` — Plain YAML for the unified config and per-service configs.
- `conformance-suite-per-protocol` — One conformance suite per protocol under the protocols module's conformance package, exposed as `rimsky conformance <protocol>`.
- `coverage-wildcard-asymmetry` — A wildcard `attribute/*` subscription covers both per-field and whole-pull reads of the same sender; a per-field subscription covers only the matching per-field read and does not cover a whole-pull read.
- `cron-robfig-v3` — The Robfig cron parser, v3 line.
- `cross-cutting-no-force-upstream-refresh` — A cross-cutting (`instance: true`) subscription carrying `force_upstream_refresh: true` is rejected at registration, because cross-cutting subscriptions are sender-agnostic and have no specific upstream to invalidate.
- `depguard-consumption-isolation` — The services module may import the protocols module only; not the foundation module, graph layer, runtime layer, or control layer.
- `depguard-foundation-internal` — External imports of the foundation module's internal package are forbidden.
- `depguard-foundation-purity` — Stdlib plus the protocols module plus chosen libs only; no graph, runtime, or control layer imports.
- `depguard-graph-purity-with-scheduler-exception` — The graph layer is pure of runtime and control layer imports, with a narrow scheduler exception.
- `depguard-pgx-isolation` — Confine the pgx Postgres driver imports to the foundation module's postgres persistence driver, the services module, the cmd group, the test-support package, and the scenario harness in the test group.
- `depguard-protocols-purity` — The protocols module imports stdlib plus generated proto bindings only.
- `depguard-runtime-purity` — The runtime layer imports the foundation module, graph layer, and protocols module only; no control layer imports.
- `design-link-annotations` — `@concept:`, `@story:`, and `@decision:` annotations at the load-bearing site link code to the design catalog.
- `doc-residue-reshape-pass` — Doc-residue cluster reshapes to GoDoc/JSDoc when above a package-level declaration; otherwise falls through to the uniform tag-or-delete rule.
- `emit-work-completed` — The terminal-application step appends a `work_completed` event pairing its `work_started` twin plus the terminal kind.
- `entry-absorption-flag` — Delegation's entry absorption is an entry-absorbed boolean on the dispatch-children input, not a pre-step.
- `event-log-kind-enum` — Operational event-log kind values are declared as a proto enum and consumed as typed values across the app layer; signal-class kinds keep their type-path discipline; persistence marshals typed at the boundary.
- `event-log-payload-shapes` — Typed oneof payloads for signal-class events; free-form JSON payload for operational events whose payload is audit data rather than typed contract.
- `exit-codes` — `0` success, `1` failure, `2` `--timeout` exceeded, `130` SIGINT during shutdown.
- `exposure-no-config` — One-shot mode is exposed only via the new verb; no operator-facing config knob.
- `fold-ownership-bail` — The verify-before-run ownership-bail path resolves through the unified claim-handle resolution engine as its own source kind.
- `force-upstream-refresh-via-receiver-keyed-map` — A receiver-keyed map of upstream node-types to proactively invalidate on receiver invalidation is built at registration from every `subscribes:` entry carrying `force_upstream_refresh: true`, with cycle detection and fan-out-target rejection at registration time.
- `graceful-shutdown` — Soft drain with hardcoded 5s SIGTERM-then-SIGKILL grace; a second SIGINT escapes to hard exit.
- `grpc-google-official` — The official Google gRPC and protobuf libraries for Go.
- `grpc-internal-protocols` — gRPC for all service-to-service protocols.
- `guard-conformance-suite` — For every mutating ownership operation, acting as the wrong supervisor changes nothing — proven identically on both drivers.
- `hard-dep-field-no-special-case` — Cascade walker and edge builder do not read any attribute-field `hard_dep:` flag; the attribute-schema validator carries no special-case rejector for that property name, and no migration-redirect error is generated.
- `hard-dep-settled-guard` — The hard-dep pull skips re-affirming an upstream that already settled this frame; the test-first reproduction confirmed the livelock and stands as the pin.
- `harness-first-ordering` — Harness hardening lands before consolidation refactors; the largest blast radius lands last.
- `http-router-chi` — The chi HTTP router, v5 line.
- `idempotency-key-header-universal` — Mandatory `Idempotency-Key` HTTP header on publisher message-emit.
- `idempotency-status-code-distinction` — `201` on fresh insert vs `200` on replay (returning the original message id).
- `image-entrypoint-role-selection` — A single entrypoint binary that runs all three roles when given no command, a single role when the command names one, and runs migrate once per deployment with the owner role determined by the command.
- `image-set-bundled-services` — One image per bundled service (eleven — sensors, stores, subscribers, executors).
- `image-set-four-core` — Four core images: the all-binaries `rimsky` image, the SQLite-defaulted all-in-one dev image, the host-agent proxy image, and the conformance runner image.
- `image-tagging-version-and-channel` — Immutable version tag plus a `:latest` (formal) or `:dev` (dev releases) channel tag.
- `image-two-stage` — Alpine Go toolchain for the build stage; distroless nonroot static base for the runtime stage.
- `implementation-language-go-plus-ts` — Go for all core code; TypeScript only in the services module's claude-agent executor.
- `instance-self-termination` — Every instance the one-shot verb creates is created with `terminate_after_run` enabled.
- `jcs-cyberphone` — The Cyberphone JCS canonicalization library.
- `launch-config-injection` — The verb writes synthetic `rimsky.yml` and `supervisor.yml` to the run dir; env vars point the role runners at them.
- `launch-integration` — Reuse the three role runners; new orchestration site under the compose verb mirrors the all-in-one entrypoint pattern.
- `layer-ordering` — Within the root module, four ordered layers — the foundation module's layer, then the graph layer, then the runtime layer, then the control layer — enforced by depguard.
- `licensing-dual-apache-agpl` — The protocols module, the claude-agent reference executor, the examples module, and the cold-read style guide are Apache-2.0; everything else is AGPL-3.0-or-later with a commercial alternative.
- `licensing-enforced-by-license-lint` — Enforced by the tools group's license-check, so Apache packages import only stdlib plus permissive plus Apache.
- `logging-slog-only` — Stdlib structured logging.
- `mechanical-cluster-sweep` — Mechanical comment-hygiene clusters (divider, commented-out-code, todo-marker, license-fragment) sweep in a dedicated pass distinct from per-site judgment.
- `memory-gate-premise-corrected` — The in-memory blob backend is gated to the single-process mode; the gate's text describes the true premise.
- `merge-validator-warnings` — Register and validate responses merge static-validator warnings into `validation_warnings`; `warnings_as_errors=true` trips on them.
- `message-idempotencies-dedup-tuple` — Dedup tuple of instance id, sender kind, sender, sender subject, and idempotency key.
- `message-sender-kind-discriminator` — The message-row sender-kind column is the three-value enum operator / publisher / instance.
- `metrics-prometheus-client` — The official Prometheus Go client library.
- `migration-direct` — The one-shot verb calls the persistence-driver migrate operation directly; no separate migrate-binary subprocess.
- `migrations-append-only-numbered` — Numbered, append-only migrations, per backend.
- `migrations-no-compat-shims` — Drop and recreate when cleaner; no compat shims.
- `module-split` — Root plus the foundation module, the protocols module, the services module, and the examples module tied by the workspace definition with local-path replaces.
- `named-lock-metric` — Named-lock acquisitions increment the acquisition metric family, labeled apart from producer claims.
- `network-binding` — One-shot control-api binds to `127.0.0.1:0` (loopback only, kernel-picked port).
- `parallel-cap-removal` — The test-all gate runs without per-module test-parallelism caps.
- `parity-expansion` — The driver-parity suite covers every queue, claim-handle, and frame behavior the runtime depends on, on both drivers.
- `peer-tls-enforcement` — The `tls` key is writable on every peer entry kind and honored at every peer dial site.
- `persistence-driver` — One-shot mode uses the existing sqlite persistence driver pointed at a per-run state.db file.
- `persistence-dual-backend` — Both Postgres and SQLite, selected by the persistence-driver config field.
- `plumb-validation-roles` — Validation-supported roles are plumbed from publisher and executor capability surfaces identically to claim producers.
- `polling-audit` — Test polls that mask ordering assumptions are converted to event-log-tail waits.
- `postgres-pgx-v5` — The pgx Postgres driver, v5 line.
- `pre-v1-break-freely` — No backwards-compat guarantee on wire, config, event-log, or resource interface pre-v1; delete dead code rather than carrying it forward.
- `producer-declared-classes-capability` — The claim-producer capabilities response carries a declared-error-classes field, stored in the discovery cache.
- `producer-error-passthrough` — The control-api error writer carries the producer's error class and message under a status distinguishing producer rejection from internal error.
- `progress-default` — Per-node lifecycle on stderr, chronologically ordered, line-buffered.
- `progress-flags` — `--quiet`, `--verbose`, `--json` flags compose the one-shot progress operating modes.
- `project-agnostic` — No code, doc, test, example, or comment names or assumes a specific consumer; templates use generic names.
- `protocol-version-v1-namespaced` — A `rimsky.v1` proto package plus all control-API HTTP routes mounted under the `/v1/` prefix, including the executor async-callback URL and the observability sub-router.
- `protojson-gateway` — The official protojson marshaling for the HTTP gateway.
- `race-gate-split` — Thin `-race -count=1` slice in test-all; full `-race -count=3` in test-race; the release chain requires it.
- `race-injection-hooks` — Deterministic injection tests at the defended concurrency seams via the post-commit hook pattern.
- `registry-hub-rimskyai-namespace` — The `rimskyai` Docker Hub namespace.
- `release-attestations` — Buildx push with max-mode provenance and SBOM attestations.
- `release-chain` — The shared release chain: lint, then license-lint, then core-images, then service-images, then test-all, then scan, then push-images.
- `release-dev-mechanical` — The dev-release flow is mechanical; no SemVer judgment, no notes, version derived as the next-minor dev pre-release with date and short SHA.
- `release-distribution` — Hub images plus npm protocols package plus Go modules plus GitHub Releases.
- `release-formal-skill` — The `/release` skill drives SemVer judgment plus notes draft plus outward push behind a single user gate.
- `release-notes-template` — Template-driven sections (Breaking / What's new / Fixes / Internal / Image set / Go module / npm); every entry traces to a diff hunk.
- `release-scan-docker-scout` — Docker Scout CVE scan gating critical and high severity against all local images.
- `release-semver-from-diff` — SemVer bump derived from diff inspection (proto, migrations, exports, CLI flags, env vars).
- `release-semver-sha-dot-joined` — The pre-release SHA is dot-joined into the SemVer pre-release segment, not appended as build metadata.
- `revive-no-exported-rule` — Disable the revive `exported` rule.
- `run-name` — Default the one-shot run name from the manifest's `project` field; `--name` overrides through the same regex.
- `service-spawn-flag` — Extend `--service <name>=<path>` (and bare-name alias form) to `rimsky compose run` via a shared spawn primitive.
- `services-source` — Extend the compose manifest schema with `executors:` and `claim_producers:` blocks; sibling unified config is a secondary source.
- `single-process-mode` — The all-in-one entrypoint's no-command path runs migrate then all three roles in one process; `RIMSKY_PROCESS_ROLE=unified` truthfully marks it.
- `spec-jcs-canonicalization` — The JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785) produces the canonical bytes for template-spec hashing.
- `sqlite-modernc-pure-go` — The modernc pure-Go SQLite driver.
- `sqlite-multiproc-safety` — Read-then-write sites are transactional and the tick/migration locks file-lock-based, so processes sharing one local file are safe; no startup gate.
- `subclaims-as-input` — Sub-claim acquisition is owned by the claim-tree machinery; the dispatch-children primitive consumes already-acquired sub-claims as input rather than calling the producer's partition-split itself.
- `subscription-edges-only-from-explicit-block` — Substitution refs do not contribute to the subscription-edge map; the map is fed by the explicit subscription block only, so cascade edges are exactly what the author wrote.
- `subscription-mounting-state` — Publisher-subscription state set `mounting | active | failed | stopped`; rows created in `mounting`; state exposed on the instance surface.
- `subscription-reconciler` — A reconciliation worker drives Subscribe for `mounting` rows with backoff and no attempt cap; `failed` is non-retryable only.
- `substitution-context-builder-reads-drained-rows` — The substitution-context builder reads drained wait-set rows; row presence is the key, irrespective of which subscription-flag combination caused the row to land.
- `substitution-grammar-closed` — The substitution grammar is a closed enumeration of data-reference tokens; cascade-shape declaration lives on the cascade-edge surface, not on the read surface.
- `substitution-grammar-fallback-routing` — Unresolved substitution refs route through fallback / lenient / optional handling at dispatch whenever a ref's wait-set row is absent, whether because the sender was out of scope or because the sender settled in the frame before the receiver entered it.
- `substitution-ref-coverage-required` — Every substitution ref in a node's attribute schema must be matched by at least one subscription entry whose sender and type would deliver the corresponding signal; registration rejects templates with uncovered refs.
- `sweep-lock-skip-on-error` — A scheduler-tick advisory-lock error is treated as lock-held: skip the sweep pass, never run unlocked.
- `termination` — The one-shot verb waits for every declared instance to reach instance-terminal state, then exits.
- `testcontainers-go` — The testcontainers-go library manages integration-test containers.
- `testing-scenario-based-e2e` — End-to-end via the test group's scenarios directory plus the services module's scenarios test directory driving the assembled product; persistence tests use testcontainers.
- `timeout-flag` — `--timeout` is opt-in with no default on the one-shot verb.
- `timestamp-format` — Run-directory timestamps use ISO 8601 UTC with colons replaced by hyphens (`YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ`).
- `tls-mode-validation` — The `tls` field is parse-time validated to exactly `off | required`; empty defaults to `off`.
- `toplevel-dirs` — The four idiomatic top-level code directories: the cmd group, the lib group, the test group, the tools group.
- `topology-test-coverage` — The services integration harness covers both the single-process all-in-one and the three-container split topology.
- `uncovered-substitution-error-shape` — Registration rejection for an uncovered substitution ref returns a structured `validation_errors` entry of kind `substitution_ref_uncovered` carrying the receiver node-type, the literal ref text, the schema property path, a copy-pasteable subscription-entry suggestion with both flags set to `false`, and a one-sentence note on the flag implications.
- `untagged-prose-by-module` — Untagged-prose sweep decomposes by top-level module root using the module-layout axis.
- `upstream-gating-at-eligibility` — A stale run is not dispatch-eligible while any subscribed upstream has an in-flight run in the same frame, propagation-path-independent.
- `uuid-google` — Google's UUID library for Go.
- `validation-error-names-mode` — Reference-validation rejections name the active mode and the config key with its relaxed settings.
- `validation-errors-additive-not-uniform` — Validation-error envelopes admit two coexisting entry shapes: a `{path, msg}` entry for simple field violations, and a structured entry carrying a `kind` discriminator plus additional fields for violations the operator needs to act on programmatically.
- `validator-learns-producer-classes` — `error_types:` keys are checked against the union of executor, producer, and `acquire/*` vocabularies; unattributable keys warn.
- `wait-set-topic-kind-taxonomy` — Five-value taxonomy (terminal, transient, attribute, event, message); `state` is admitted as a defensive fallback for unrecognized rows.
- `wake-on-change-wait-set-only` — A matching subscription edge with `wake_on_change: true` inserts a wait-set row for the receiver on the sender's run and stale-marks the receiver; with `wake_on_change: false` the row is inserted but the receiver is not stale-marked, and when there is no in-flight receiver run at the sender's settle the row is skipped.
- `wire-commit-response-fields` — Base Commit `version_id` is persisted to the claim-handle row; `producer_metadata` surfaces in the fan-out parent's writeback.
- `yaml-gopkg-v3` — The yaml.v3 YAML parser library.
